# A test's cached result survives a change to the build's cache plumbing. The
# variables naming the cache log and the cache's owner, and the build cache's
# own directory, are not inputs to the test, though the test reads all three.

env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache
env GOCACHELOG=$WORK/log1
go test -run=TestReadsPlumbing .
stdout '^ok\s+m\s+[0-9.]+s$'

env GOCACHELOG=$WORK/log2
cp marker.txt $WORK/gocache/marker.txt
go test -run=TestReadsPlumbing .
stdout '^ok\s+m\s+\(cached\)$'

# A variable outside the plumbing is still an input.
env SOME_INPUT=changed
go test -run=TestReadsPlumbing .
stdout '^ok\s+m\s+[0-9.]+s$'

# A module cache path is keyed by its name, which carries the version. A
# version missing on one run and downloaded by the next changes nothing.
env GOMODCACHE=$WORK/modcache
go test -run=TestReadsModCache .
stdout '^ok\s+m\s+[0-9.]+s$'
mkdir $WORK/modcache/example.com/vectors@v1.0.0
cp marker.txt $WORK/modcache/example.com/vectors@v1.0.0/vectors.json
go test -run=TestReadsModCache .
stdout '^ok\s+m\s+\(cached\)$'

-- go.mod --
module m

go 1.27
-- marker.txt --
an entry the first run did not see
-- m_test.go --
package m

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

func TestReadsPlumbing(t *testing.T) {
	os.Getenv("GOCACHELOG")
	os.Getenv("GO_BUILDCACHE_BROKER")
	os.Getenv("SOME_INPUT")
	dir := os.Getenv("GOCACHE")
	if _, err := os.ReadDir(dir); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "marker.txt"))
}

func TestReadsModCache(t *testing.T) {
	dir := filepath.Join(os.Getenv("GOMODCACHE"), "example.com", "vectors@v1.0.0")
	os.Stat(dir)
	os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "vectors.json"))
}
